Surami Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Surami, Georgia

Not demolished. Surami, an ancient trading town on the route between Tbilisi and western Georgia, had documented Jewish presence from the early-to-mid 18th century; just 13 families lived there by the early 19th century, growing to support 2-3 synagogues by the 1930s (only one active during the Soviet era, built in stone in 1911, drawing up to 300 worshippers on holidays). Surami holds a unique connection to the 'Bible of Breti' - the famous 1513 manuscript from Breti (a town in Shida Kartli) - which Breti's Jews brought with them when they relocated to Surami in the mid-19th century; the original handwritten copy was later rediscovered in Surami and now resides in Georgia's National Manuscript Center. This cemetery, on a hillside near the highway, held burials from the 1880s through 2020.
